Saab reports sea trials of a large uncrewed underwater demonstrator

The project with FMV and the Swedish Armed Forces reached sea trials less than a year after contract award.

Saab ↗16 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

A completed demonstrator phase

On October 16, Saab said its Large Uncrewed Underwater Vehicle project with FMV and the Swedish Armed Forces had completed its first phase. Development, construction and sea trials took less than a year from contract award. This is a demonstrator used to evaluate technology.

A shared autonomy layer

The vehicle integrates Saab’s Autonomous Ocean Core with submarine-design and sensor-integration expertise. The control system supports autonomous surface and subsurface vehicles; this demonstrator is intended to help evaluate operations alongside existing naval platforms.

Further development ahead

The next phase is expected to advance software, sensors and autonomy, informing Swedish acquisition and operational decisions. The announcement gives no range, depth or endurance figures and does not confirm entry into operational service or volume production.
